title: login-from-anywhere: sso, identity, permissions, jira coverage

claims.text: Culture Nodes is reachable at nodes.culture.dev behind Cloudflare Access SSO on the same Zero Trust team as chat.agentculture.org; every person who signs in is a named human actor and every agent or bridge holds its own API token, and the ledger stamps origin from the authenticated caller rather than a request field; a ticket's human tasks, proposed claims and confirmations are decided on its own page under that identity; agents can read a Jira ticket's body, comments and links, and the system moves the board itself: In Review on a PR, Waiting on a parked question, Done on merge. OIDC / Entra workload auth is scoped as the follow-on.

honesty_conditions.text: Each clause of the announcement maps to a confirmed requirement with a measured success signal in c29; the delivery summary lists any clause that did not ship as not shipped, never as partially true

claims.text: The SSO front is Cloudflare Access on team agentculture.cloudflareaccess.com, provisioned like chat.agentculture.org: one cultureflare remote-login setup run (hostname nodes.culture.dev, service pointed at thor's API port, allow policy listing the operator's email, --apply) creates the tunnel, CNAME, Access app and allow-by-email policy; the tunnel runs as a token-mode systemd user unit (the cloudflared-chat.service shape on spark, reading TUNNEL_TOKEN_FILE), never a config.yml on the API host

claims.text: The control plane verifies the Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion header the way irc-lens web/auth.py does — RS256 against the team's /cdn-cgi/access/certs JWKS, audience pinned to the Access app AUD, issuer pinned to the team domain, kid-miss refetch with an anti-flood window — and maps the email claim (interactive SSO) or common_name claim (service token) to a registered actor; the Go runtime does this with the standard library (crypto/rsa, encoding/json, net/http), honouring the zero-third-party-dependency rule

honesty_conditions.text: A Go test verifies a token signed by a test RSA key against a fake JWKS endpoint: valid passes; wrong aud, wrong iss, expired, unknown kid (after one refetch) and bad signature each refuse with a named reason; no non-stdlib import appears in internal/auth

claims.text: Cloudflare Access is the ONLY human login surface: no OAuth client, session cookie, password or user table lives in the control plane; identity arrives as a verified JWT claim and the control plane only decides which registered actor it maps to. OIDC/Entra token validation for API callers and workload callbacks (#6, docs/decisions/issue-6-oidc-workload-authentication.md) stays the named follow-on issue, not this cycle's build
